title: Chain Spaces and Corners
description: Use chain spaces to create gaps, corners, and easy landing points for taller stitches.

content.summary: Chain spaces create structure in motifs and lacy rows by giving you a space to work into instead of only a top loop.
content.whyItMatters: Granny-style projects, flowers, and many decorative patterns depend on reading and using chain spaces correctly.
steps: Work a few chain stitches to create a gap between stitch groups.
On the next row or round, place stitches into the chain space instead of forcing them into each individual chain.
Use larger chain spaces at corners so the fabric can turn cleanly.
Look for the open gap itself, not just the top loops, when deciding where to place the next group.
content.practice: Make a small sample with chain spaces between stitch groups and repeat one more row into those spaces.
commonMistakes: Working into the wrong stitch beside the gap instead of into the actual chain space.
Making corner spaces too tight, which causes motifs to buckle inward.
